reason: The PROBLEM is real and I verified every claim by driving the master; the FIX is wrong in its load-bearing half, so the finding is refuted with the fix corrected below. Verified at 1440/1280/768/390 (motion=settled): in state=first-run the plot is 686px wide (the finding says ~660 - immaterial), 168px tall, holds one .colw, gridlines resolve to [] against ["6","12"] in every state that draws this chart, one x-label "13 Jul", a full-width baseline, and a 22px bar whose centre sits at 343px of 686 - dead centre. Source line 782 confirms the height is a typed literal: --h:60 on both the bar and its bar-val, twice, while every other column on this surface goes through pct(v, max). The consequence is real too: D.thisWeek is 12 and the twelve-week chart draws 12 at pct(12,12)=100 (168px), so the same value is 101px here and 168px there in identical mark grammar. The behaviour gate does NOT already cover this - its "the chart states its own scale" assertion runs on state=full only, so this is the state the gate skips, not a restatement of it. Class confirmed as defect, not raised: nothing on the first-run frame gives the bar a magnitude to be wrong against (no axis, no gridline, no sibling column), and the value is printed in words twice, so the surface does not assert an untruth - it is visibly wrong and passable. WHY THE FIX FAILS. "Derive the single bar height from that scale (12 against a max of 12)" is circular: with one datum the max IS the datum, so the bar renders at 100% for any value whatsoever - a literal 100 replacing a literal 60, encoding exactly as little. It is also actively worse, because a bar landing on a gridline labelled 12 reads as a ceiling reached, planting a comparative claim in the one state whose own copy refuses comparison ("Four weeks of records make a comparison worth printing. Yours arrive on 10 August."). The second half of the fix - faint placeholder slots for the eleven weeks that have not happened - collides with two protected objects: faint marks on the baseline of a completions chart are indistinguishable from eleven weeks of zero, which is the honest-degradation contract, and the drawn-but-empty ghost plot in movement three already owns "this is the chart we would draw". Only the narrow-the-plot option survives.
sharpenedFix: Keep the narrowing, drop the invented scale. (1) In first-run give the plot a fixed width of one to three real column slots rather than 100% - the twelve-week pitch at 1440 is 686/12 = 57px, so roughly 57-171px - left-aligned in the chart area with the baseline running only under that width, so the mark stands at the physical width and pitch it will hold when the twelve-week chart arrives instead of floating in 686px of empty plot. (2) Add NO gridlines and derive NO max from the single datum, for the reason above; the magnitude stays where it already is and is already correct, in the hero numeral and the "12 so far" datum label. (3) Bind the height through pct() rather than a typed literal only once a non-self-referential max exists (i.e. when four weeks of records arrive and the state stops being first-run); until then the honest statement is that there is no scale, and the composition should stop borrowing the visual grammar of one. (4) Keep the hatched, open-topped bar and the "so far" label untouched - both are protected and both are asserted by the behaviour gate. (5) Independently of this finding and found while measuring it: the first-run chart has no spoken equivalent at all (p.sr present in full, absent in first-run), so this mark is silent to a screen reader while the twelve-week chart is not - add the one-sentence sr line.
breaks: WHAT IT BREAKS. The behaviour gate reads the partial bucket via .plot .colw:last-child .bar plus .bar-val; a narrowed plot must still expose exactly one .colw with the gradient background, border-bottom 0 and a "so far" label or that assertion fails - re-run interaction-check.mjs. .bar-val is left:50% translateX(-50%) with white-space:nowrap, so "12 so far" (about 90px) will overhang both edges of a 57px plot; re-measure its box against the card padding at 1440/1280/768/390, and do not inherit the existing precedent - in state=full at 1440 that same label already collides with the top gridline value (bar-val sits 21px ABOVE the plot top and overlaps the "12" in light-full--1440x960.png), which is a separate unresolved defect. .hero is grid-template-columns minmax(220px,300px) 1fr and collapses to a single track at 768 and below (measured tracks: 300px+686px at 1440 and 1280, 566px at 768, 308px at 390), so a fixed narrow plot needs an explicit decision at 390 where the whole chart is only 308px - a 57px plot leaves a large dead right edge inside the card. Card height is unchanged (the plot stays 168px), so the vertical whitespace under the hero sentence is not fixed by this and should be judged again after. RE-MEASURE AFTER: interaction-check.mjs in full, audit.mjs for the lab, and re-shoot light-first-run--1440x960.png plus the 390/768/1280 frames, since nothing below the hero card moves but every frame that feeds the gates carries this card.
